reviews.title: Zero Accountability
reviews.text:
I was a dedicated Valvoline customer for years. My family’s vehicles were all serviced there without issue — until my last visit, which was an absolute disaster.

After an oil change at the Valvoline in Johnston, RI, my hood flew open on the highway. The result was a $9,000 insurance claim. Valvoline denied all liability, insisting their bay video showed the technician “closing the hood per policy.”

I’ve seen the video myself, obtained through my insurance company, and that claim is simply false. The footage clearly shows the tech dropping my hood from about 4 inches and giving it a quick lift up. That is not the way to close a hood. A proper hood latch engagement requires a 12-inch drop to fully engage the mechanism. This hood was closed gingerly, not correctly — and the consequences were severe.

My insurance paid the claim, but I’ve asked Valvoline to at least cover my $1,000 deductible as a basic gesture of good faith. Let’s be honest: this incident would not have happened if I hadn’t been in their bay that day. Covering roughly 10% of the damage — the part directly tied to their mistake — is the bare minimum any responsible company should do.

Valvoline chose not to. And that tells me everything I need to know about how they value their customers.
